verses.text: While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees came up to them.
They were very upset because the apostles were teaching the people and saying that through Jesus the dead will rise.
They arrested Peter and John and, because it was already evening, they kept them in jail until the next day.
But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men who believed grew to about five thousand.
The next day the rulers, the elders, and the teachers of the law met in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there, and so were Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and the other men of the high priest's family.
They had Peter and John stand in front of them and asked, "By what power or in what name did you do this?"
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers and elders of the people,
today you are asking us about a kind thing we did for a man who could not walk. You want to know how he was healed.
Then all of you and all the people of Israel should know this: this man stands before you healed by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. You nailed him to a cross, but God raised him from the dead.
Jesus is 'the stone you builders rejected, which has become the most important stone of the building.'
Salvation is found in no one else. There is no other name under heaven given to people by which we must be saved."
The leaders saw how bold Peter and John were, and they knew they were ordinary men with no schooling. They were amazed, and they realised that these men had been with Jesus.
They could also see the man who had been healed standing there with them, so there was nothing they could say against it.
So they ordered them to leave the council room, and then talked it over among themselves.
They said, "What should we do with these men? Everyone living in Jerusalem knows they have done an amazing miracle, and we cannot deny it.
But to stop this from spreading any further among the people, we must warn them not to speak to anyone in this name again."
So they called them back in and ordered them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered, "You decide which is right in God's eyes: to obey you, or to obey God.
We cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard."
After more threats, they let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, because all the people were praising God for what had happened.
The man who had been healed by this miracle was more than forty years old.
After they were set free, Peter and John went back to their own people and told them everything the chief priests and elders had said.
When they heard it, they all prayed to God together: "Lord, you made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
By the Holy Spirit you spoke through our ancestor David, your servant: 'Why do the nations rage? Why do the peoples make useless plans?
The kings of the earth get ready to fight, and the rulers come together against the Lord and against his Christ.'
"It is true. Herod and Pontius Pilate met together in this city with the Gentiles and the people of Israel. They came together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you chose.
They did what your power and your plan had already decided should happen.
Now, Lord, see how they threaten us. Help your servants to speak your word very boldly.
Stretch out your hand to heal, and let signs and wonders be done through the name of your holy servant Jesus."
After they prayed, the place where they were meeting shook. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God's word boldly.
All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one said that anything they owned was their own. They shared everything they had.
With great power the apostles kept telling people that the Lord Jesus had risen from the dead. And God's grace was on all of them.
There was no one in need among them. From time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money,
and put it at the apostles' feet. Then it was given to anyone who had need.
Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, was called Barnabas by the apostles. That name means Son of Encouragement.
He sold a field he owned, brought the money, and put it at the apostles' feet.
